symptom: ako/mxcli#888 review: under mdl 1, `create or modify` that grows a stored flow by a guard at the start of an `if` branch (`if $N > 5 then if $N > 10 then return true; end if; log …; end if;`) was refused: "there is no free room for the return at (660, 350): its branch would be drawn across the flow from the ExclusiveSplit '$N > 5' at (360, 200) to the ActionActivity at (770, 300)". Nothing would have crossed. Separately, a fragment whose error handler states `return false;` was refused with advice to "end that path with a return".
cause: checkBranches (mdl/backend/mfmutator/splice.go) tested the fragment's return branch against every stored sequence flow, including the flow the insert goes on. After makeRoom shifts the branch's first activity along, that flow's old centre-to-centre line runs diagonally through the return's branch area — but the splice re-points it at the fragment's entry, so the line it was checked as never exists. The error-handler message assumed only a handler without a return reaches that refusal; a handler's return is drawn by addTerminalEndEventForPendingHandler, not addEndEventWithReturn, so it is not in returnEndIDs either.
fix: checkRoom/checkBranches take onFlow (the insert's flow id, passed from makeRoom) and skip it, as Replace already skips the replaced node's flows. The cutFragment refusal now says an inserted error handler has to rejoin and that a return inside an error handler is not spliced yet.
test: mdl/roundtrip/flow_splice_guard_test.go TestSpliceRerun_GrowBranchByGuard (parity suite; twice-exec Unchanged, every decision out-flow cased); reverting the onFlow skip fails it with the reported refusal, while TestSpliceRerun_GrowByGuardAcrossAFlowIsRefused still refuses its genuine crossing. mdl/executor/cmd_alter_flow_cut_test.go for the message. TestApp copy: grow-in-branch on mxcli-authored and on Studio Pro-authored WorkflowCommons.ACT_WorkflowComment_Edit (plus a condition change), rerun and fresh-describe re-exec Unchanged, mx check 0 errors.
insight: A geometry check run before a splice sees the graph as it is, not as it will be: the flows the splice rewires must be excluded (or checked as rewired), or the check refuses its own work. Test a new placement check with the fragment in a branch, not only on the main line.
